name: Ente Locker
insteadOf: Storing IDs and documents in the cloud
hook: An end-to-end encrypted locker for your passports, IDs, insurance, and important documents.
bullets: End-to-end encrypted vault for documents, IDs, and secure notes
Available on mobile and the web, with everything kept private
Family sharing so the people who need access can get it
Built on the same open-source stack as Ente Photos and Ente Auth
benefits: A digital safe for the documents you'd never put in a random cloud drive
End-to-end encryption means only you can open your locker
Stop hunting for scanned IDs across email and your camera roll
Share critical documents with family without losing control of them
setupSteps: Install Ente Locker on your phone (or open it on the web)
Create an account — the same Ente login works across the suite
Add documents, IDs, and notes to your locker
Organize items and share a locker with family if you want
details: Ente Locker is an end-to-end encrypted vault from the makers of Ente Photos and Ente Auth, designed to hold the sensitive documents you shouldn't scatter across email, cloud drives, and your camera roll — passports, IDs, insurance papers, medical records, and secure notes. Everything is encrypted on your device so only you can open it, and the app is available on mobile and the web with the same account used across the rest of the Ente suite. You can organize items, add files and notes, and share a locker with family members who need access to critical documents. Like the rest of Ente, it's open source (AGPL-3.0), cross-platform, and can be self-hosted if you'd rather run it yourself.
